messages:
samantha_support: customer reports recurring failures when using fn/tool calling in JSON mode. error from runtime: \"Invalid JSON payload: unexpected token \\\" in string\". they say they are passing structured args (object) via our JS SDK v0.9.2 and sometimes it works, sometimes the runtime rejects it. stack: prod-us-east.

samantha_support: attaching the request/response pair they pasted (sanitized):

samantha_support: REQUEST (from customer):
```json
{
  \"model\": \"open-compat-1\",
  \"input\": \"call tool calculate_cart\",
  \"function_call\": {
    \"name\": \"calculate_cart\",
    \"arguments\": {
      \"user_id\": \"acct_123\",
      \"order_ids\": [\"ord_1\", \"ord_2\"]
    }
  }
}
```

samantha_support: RUNTIME LOG (from customer):
```
ERROR: validation failed for fncall args: invalid json at offset 12
raw_payload: \"{\\\"user_id\\\":\\\"acct_123\\\",\\\"order_ids\\\":\\\"[\\\"ord_1\\\",\\\"ord_2\\\"]\\\"}\"
```

samantha_support: note: see how order_ids ended up as a stringified array inside the arguments? customer says they never stringify arrays.

erik_runtime: :eyes: hmm looks like we received arguments as a JSON string (double-encoded). runtime expects arguments to be an object but the payload shows arguments were serialized to a string earlier. do we have any recent changes in strict/jsonmode parsing?

olga_sdk: we shipped a patch in v0.9.2 that toggles a legacy fetch fallback for some browser environments. that fallback does manual body handling and in rare cases calls JSON.stringify on nested objects when Content-Type is missing.

olga_sdk: quick check: did customer set Content-Type: application/json on the request? if not, the fallback will treat body as form-like and stringify nested arrays.

samantha_support: customer confirms they are using a third-party proxy that strips content-type sometimes. they also reported higher error rates during traffic spikes.

dave_oncall: sounds like two possible vectors: (1) proxy dropping content-type -> SDK fallback stringifies and double-encodes arrays, (2) model/tool output including an escaped JSON blob which then gets passed through runtime with no normalization. need repro.

repro-bot: minimal repro steps suggested:
1) run curl without Content-Type header against /v1/chat.completions (or our fncall endpoint) using body:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete -d '{"model":"open-compat-1","function_call":{"name":"calculate_cart","arguments":{"user_id":"acct_123","order_ids":["ord_1","ord_2"]}}}'
```
2) observe runtime logs for stringified array in arguments.

olga_sdk: workaround options for customer: pin SDK to v0.9.1 (no fallback behavior) OR explicitly set header Content-Type: application/json on proxy. we'll prepare a small patch to detect stringified arrays and attempt to parse them before sending to runtime as a short-term mitigation.

erik_runtime: on runtime side we can make arg parsing more permissive: if arguments is a string and it parses as JSON, accept it (and emit a telemetry flag). low-risk change, but we should add a metric so we can rollback if unexpected. I'll open an RFC.

dave_oncall: priority: P2 for immediate customer impact. please gather: sdk version, proxy vendor, sample failing request id, and a small repro. support to collect and reply to customer with recommended header fix and temporary pin.

samantha_support: collecting request ids now (cust gave req ids: req_2024-11-21_abc123, req_2024-11-21_def456). I'll reply with pin + header steps and link to our repro snippet.

olga_sdk: follow-up: filing SDK issue and draft changelog note. will also add an opt-in lenient-parse flag for customers who cannot control proxies.

erik_runtime: I'll prototype the permissive-parse and add a histogram for \"args_received_type\" (object|string/invalid) and a counter for \"args_double_encoded_detected\".

samantha_support: thanks all. I'll update customer and keep this thread for rollback notes. :thumbsup:

dave_oncall: tagging eng-runtime and sdk for visibility. escalation ok to eng if repeat failures after header mitigation. :triage:
